identity.fresh_complete_source_build: NOT RUN; reused SDK/dependencies/objects with seven separately compiled replacements

upstream_primary_sources.scope: Reported aarch64-softmmu raspi3ap SD-read reproduction on SDK 3.1.50, trapping in fiber rewind. Raising Asyncify/per-fiber buffers did not solve that reproduction. This is a different guest/board from Xtensa StackChan.

The reporter attributes issue48 to a 64KiB pthread shadow stack overflowing into its coroutine-current TLS, and proposes 2MiB QEMU thread stacks plus 4MiB main stack. This author diagnosis is not an accepted proof of universal JIT/Asyncify incompatibility, nor a StackChan validation result. The stack-size changes are not included in this candidate.

maintenance_delta.measurement: git apply --numstat on the exact candidate host-backend patch; current snapshot includes diagnostic fixes beyond the earlier approximate inventory.
maintenance_delta.classification: Substantial new QEMU host CPU backend; same Xtensa frontend/SoC model, but not a small patch to production TCI.

execution_differences: The wasm32 host backend fixes TCG_TARGET_REG_BITS at 64. Production TCI selects 32 on the wasm32 host.
JIT0 executes the backend fork of the TCI interpreter and its direct-TLB RAM load/store path. It is not the production 32-bit TCI control.
JIT1 compiles hot TCG blocks into additional Worker-local WebAssembly modules importing the actual QEMU helper functions and the shared linear memory.

A same-artifact JIT0/JIT1 pair can isolate hot-block compilation within this candidate. A comparison against production also contains register-width, interpreter, direct-TLB, host-backend, and build differences.

The shared-source comparison covers 160 recorded files and found only meson.build different in that set. It does not cover away the explicitly added/changed CPU-backend files or prove their semantics.

asyncify_source_observations.finding: instantiate_wasm imports wasmTable helper entries and reads this Worker Asyncify.state via helper.u. Fresh wasmMemory.buffer views are used for module/import reads.
Generated continuation blocks use a module-global block index so rewind can resume the helper-containing block.
General helpers record helper return-PC and continuation block, call the imported helper, then return early when Asyncify reports Unwinding.
The slow qemu_ld helper path records its block boundary and checks Unwinding after the imported load helper.
The slow qemu_st helper path likewise records a block boundary and checks Unwinding.
The shared existing coroutine switch updates current/action and calls the SDK emscripten_fiber_swap; the new gate only controls diagnostics.
The inherited main cpu_exec_setjmp restores the saved C shadow stack after SjLj before normal cleanup. This does not prove every alternate atomic or nested longjmp path.
Fiber switching restores stack limits/pointer and drives the Unwinding/Rewinding state machine. Level2 stack checking updates current fiber limits.
Generated invoke wrappers save/restore the shadow stack around the numeric SjLj exception. Dynamic generated modules are not automatically a proof of arbitrary exception or rewind correctness.

diagnostic_decision.allowed_scope: Read-only review found no definite condition requiring cancellation of the isolated same-candidate JIT0/JIT1 Factory diagnostic. This is not a guarantee of safety, correctness, speed, or stability.
diagnostic_decision.stack_policy: Candidate retains inherited main/default pthread64KiB and STACK_OVERFLOW_CHECK=2, without PR50 or SDK changes. An actual stack trap is a failed diagnostic, not grounds to suppress checks.
diagnostic_decision.failure_policy: Preserve CompileError, Asyncify trap, stack guard, watchdog timeout, Double exception, reset, and cleanup failure as failures. Do not inherit an older firmware, board, backend, or native PASS.
remaining_specific_risks: Actual shadow-stack demand can exceed64KiB, especially nested synchronous block I/O and coroutine completion.
Nested helper/fiber/rewind paths, complex and i128 helper ABI, and longjmp through generated modules have not been exhaustively executed.
A coroutine resumed on a different Worker has thread-local SDK/continuation hazards; migration/re-entry requires explicit support or a clear rejection boundary.
Direct-TLB page, alignment, permission, MMIO, and exception-PC behavior differs from production helper-only access paths and needs equivalence evidence.
Concurrent memory growth, generated-module GC, TB invalidation/remap/SMC, and Worker-slot lifecycle remain stress gates.

ctpop.method: host C emitter and actual WebAssembly.Module/Instance execution
ctpop.positive: Corrected actual dispatch/emitter code produces valid Wasm and all8vectors pass for both32/64bit cases.
ctpop.negative: Original64bit path reads the wrong operands; original and operand-only32bit paths fail Wasm type validation until unsigned i32-to-i64 extension is added.
limits: Subset extraction uses stub TCG context/opcode enum and output buffer; actual dispatcher cases, paired TCI/Wasm ctpop functions and Wasm opcode emitters are retained.
This validates ctpop operand/type corrections, not the complete backend instruction set or Xtensa firmware.

memory_growth.method: actual extracted EM_JS bodies with real WebAssembly.Memory.grow and Module/Instance execution
memory_growth.positive: Three fresh-view cases pass after real shared WebAssembly.Memory.grow and module/instance execution.
memory_growth.negative: Three old-view cases fail: byte buffer empty, import DataView range, and post-grow registered callback range.
limits: addFunction and finalization registration are host fixtures; actual module compilation/instantiation and memory growth run in Node WebAssembly.
GC callback is invoked explicitly after real growth; browser GC scheduling and concurrent growth remain separate stress gates.

minimum_additional_product_gates.required: Execute generated-Wasm versus a reference oracle for all enabled operations and both register widths, including high bits, zero, signed extrema, shifts/rotates, carry/borrow/sub2, ctpop and division edges. Exercise helper argument/return types, register spill boundary, pointer/i32/i64/i128 packing and signedness.

Same-guest differential tests for signed/unsigned endian loads/stores, aligned/unaligned and cross-page accesses, RAM/ROM/MMIO, permissions and fault addresses/PCs, TLB flush/remap and aliases. Exercise real memory barriers, atomic paths and two-vCPU message passing, retaining the I/O can_do_io guard.

Run self-modifying code and executable mapping changes on both vCPUs; invalidate/regenerate shared TBs while each Worker owns its compiled instance and jump links. Stress eviction/GC, slot bounds, fresh VM/module-cache restarts and stop with zero owned live Workers.

Verify precise IO recompile counts1/2, atomic fallback, replay/watchpoint/SMC exact-next flags, helper longjmp fault-PC recovery, Xtensa window overflow/underflow and nested interrupt levels. Repeat timer/WDT and Factory faults without changing guest clocks, IRQ priority, watchdog or reset semantics.

With real SDK3.1.50 and inherited guards, execute C-to-generated-module-to-C helper-to-block-I/O/fiber unwind/rewind, void/nonvoid returns and longjmp at nested points. Check state, arguments and shadow-stack limits after resume; cover repeated switches, same-Worker re-entry and explicitly supported/rejected cross-Worker migration.

A reproducible fresh source/SDK build with locked CPU-backend patches and artifacts, bounded memory/compile/GC behavior, samecandidate JIT0/JIT1 stability pairs, and all admitted firmware/board/controller/input/frame/serial/cleanup gates on the exact final artifact. Include unknown/default firmware compatibility and longer stability runs; a single Factory success cannot establish overall product stability.

redaction: No firmware/ROM bytes, credentials, private endpoints, host paths, target/session identifiers, raw heap/stack addresses or raw logs are included.
